# kmtest conformance baseline — parse_kmtest_serial.py format
# arch=arm64  generated by `vibeos-cli conformance --arch arm64 --write-baseline`
# KeEvent re-seeded 2026-09-12, 42733 -> 42601, by HAND and deliberately NOT by
#   `--write-baseline`. The MP kernel became the default boot that day, and
#   KeEvent.c:85 excludes its `Wait=TRUE` block when KmtIsMultiProcessorBuild is
#   true (the test's manual cleanup would leave the MP dispatcher lock held). The
#   delta is arithmetic, not a sample: 3 IRQLs x 2 event types x 2 operations x 11
#   assertions in CheckEvent = 132, exactly, and all three arches report the same
#   42601. A wholesale re-seed was tried first and REVERTED -- it re-rolls every
#   row from one sweep, which collapsed 5 `assert?` bistable marks into `assert`
#   (freezing one boot's face into the floor, the thing `--only` exists to
#   prevent) and deleted this file's own provenance comments. Prefer a hand edit
#   with a reason over a wholesale rewrite whenever the change is understood.
# IoInterrupt identities moved 119/120 -> 129/130 on 2026-09-12: a pure RENAME,
#   not a new failure. The baseline addresses assertions by file:line, and a
#   10-line explanatory comment added above them in IoInterrupt.c shifted every
#   identity below it. Editing any kmtest file invalidates the assert identities
#   beneath the edit -- check for that before reading one as a regression.
# 2026-10-03, by HAND: arm64 now boots the livecd file set like x86 (/MININT, setup
#   -mini, DHCP and the netsvcs services all running). Three rows moved with it:
#   NtSystemDebugControl 36/6 -> 22/20 (+ :165): /MININT sets InitIsWinPEMode, which
#     routes SysDbg commands 7-20 to KdSystemDebugControl. The row is now amd64's,
#     byte for byte -- parity, not a regression.
#   MmMdl 575 -> 569: TestMmAllocatePagesForMdl allocates MDLs until memory runs out,
#     so its assert count tracks free pages, and more is running now. A master batch
#     had already shown 569 once.
#   ExFastMutex floor 209 -> 204, :283-:315 bistable: every one of them is
#     TestFastMutexConcurrent's race -- a freshly created thread must reach the mutex
#     and block inside StartThread's 50 ms timeout, or Count/Contention lag one
#     waiter behind. :298/:304 were already banked failures on master; with more
#     running in the guest, WHICH step loses the race now varies from sweep to sweep
#     (six full-media sweeps: 204-208, a different subset each time).
# 2026-10-08, by HAND (rows only, per-arch samples all identical): banked a month of
#   unbanked gains -- ExHardError 24/6 -> 30/0, IoVolume 1 -> 7 (ExResource stays 845 on purpose,
#   c92ea2a: 879 minus the 34 checks its race can cost),
#   ObSecurity 694 -> 695, RtlRangeList -> 5xx and the rest below. And ObTypes is now a
#   .cpp (upstream, synced 2026-09-21): the parser only matched `<file>.c:<line>`, so its
#   identities had silently vanished from every sweep since. The row now carries the
#   ObTypes.cpp identities -- a rename plus two newly-passing asserts, not new failures.
#   ExFastMutex 204/10 -> 219/0, and its :283-:315 bistable marks are retired: :57-:133
#   and :283/:304 were a real HAL bug (ExAcquire/ExTryToAcquireFastMutex stored OldIrql
#   before owning the mutex), and :294/:298 were setup.exe's COM registration burst
#   starving the 50 ms races; kmtest-sweep now waits for setup.exe to exit.
# 2026-10-08 (later), by HAND, two agreeing sweeps: MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache and
#   MmReservedMapping come out of quarantine after their kernel bugs were fixed (see the
#   sweep list).
